title: Satellite operators emphasize launch deals in a constrained market
summary: Satellite operators are highlighting secured launch deals despite uncertainty in availability due to a constrained launch market. They are reassuring investors and customers about their launch capacity commitments.

title: U.S. defense agencies tap three companies for satellite disposal study
summary: U.S. defense agencies have selected Firefly, D-Orbit USA, and Katalyst to compete in a study on satellite disposal methods. The goal is to explore commercial solutions for capturing and removing aging spacecraft.

title: Lunar orbiter among upcoming NASA CLPS task orders
summary: NASA plans to award three more lunar missions this year through its Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program, including a replacement for the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. The missions are part of ongoing efforts to support lunar exploration and scientific research.

title: U.S. Space Force adds second surveillance sensor to Japanese constellation
summary: The U.S. Space Force has added a second surveillance sensor to the Japanese Quasi-Zenith Satellite System (QZSS) constellation with the launch of QZS-7 on Aug. 10. This marks the completion of a bilateral program to host U.S. sensors aboard Japanese navigation satellites.

title: Wallops gears up for an increase in launches
summary: Wallops Island is preparing for a significant increase in launches, prompting calls for infrastructure improvements to support growing activity. Companies and officials emphasize the need for upgrades to accommodate the surge.

title: Spire and PlanetiQ win NOAA radio-occultation contracts
summary: NOAA awarded contracts to Spire Global and PlanetiQ for radio occultation data to enhance terrestrial and space weather forecasts. The contracts support NOAA's weather prediction capabilities.

title: Cheaper launch has moved the spacecraft bottleneck. Mass is out, surface area is in.
summary: Cheaper launch costs have shifted the primary constraint in spacecraft design from mass to surface area. This change reflects the reduced impact of mass on spaceflight expenses.

title: Blue Origin outlines plans for second Cape Canaveral launch pad
summary: Blue Origin announced plans to expand its Florida launch site by adding a second pad for a larger version of New Glenn. The company aims to rebuild and expand its Cape Canaveral launch facilities.

title: Intuitive Machines wins contract for three GEO satellites
summary: Intuitive Machines secured a $600 million contract to build three geostationary orbit communications satellites for an undisclosed customer. The deal marks a significant expansion in the company's satellite business.

title: Bulgaria advances project to launch new space, defense innovation hub
summary: Bulgaria's government approved a draft memorandum with EnduroSat to develop a new space and defense innovation hub. The collaboration aims to advance the country's space and defense capabilities.

title: How to watch 'Lanterns' — HBO's gritty new Green Lantern show
summary: HBO released a new gritty space cop mystery series titled 'Lanterns' featuring Green Lantern characters Hal Jordan and John Stewart. The show is described as a hardboiled take on the classic superhero franchise.

title: NASA funds spherical 'Aerobots' that could explore the caves of Saturn's moon Titan
summary: NASA has funded a project for spherical 'Aerobots' designed to explore caves on Saturn's moon Titan, drawing inspiration from the Mars Ingenuity helicopter. This early-stage grant aims to demonstrate the feasibility of aerial exploration in Titan's unique environment.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 16, 1963: Wingless M2-F1 completes 1st glide flight
summary: NASA's M2-F1 aircraft prototype, a wingless lifting body, completed its first glide flight on August 16, 1963. This experimental aircraft was a precursor to future space shuttle designs.

title: Artemis II pilot thanks NASA for letting him fly Orion by hand: 'I'm still blown away by that trust'
summary: The Artemis II crew expressed gratitude to NASA and its contractors during a public event in Colorado, highlighting the trust placed in them to manually pilot the Orion spacecraft. The crew spoke to a crowd of over 8,000 at Red Rocks Amphitheatre on Aug. 3, 2026.

title: 'This goes beyond showcasing technological soft power': China's new moon map signals bold space ambitions (video)
summary: China has released a new moon map with updated chronology and data about the lunar far side, introducing a homegrown cartographic standard. This development is seen as a demonstration of China's technological prowess and ambitions in mapping the solar system.

title: Stomp Rockets: The perfect start to model rocketry for kids?
summary: Stomp Rockets are introduced as an ideal beginner's model rocketry kit for children. It aims to spark interest in model rocketry through an accessible and engaging activity.

title: New record! SpaceX launches 2 Falcon 9 rockets just 38 minutes apart (video)
summary: SpaceX set a new spaceflight record by launching two Falcon 9 rockets just 38 minutes apart on August 15. This achievement highlights the company's rapid launch capabilities.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 15, 1977: Mysterious 'Wow!' Signal boosts search for E.T.
summary: On Aug. 15, 1977, astronomers detected the unexplained 'Wow!' signal using Ohio State University's Big Ear radio telescope, which remains a mystery in the search for extraterrestrial life.

title: 'Lanterns': Who's who in HBO's Green Lantern show?
summary: The news discusses the cast of HBO's upcoming Green Lantern show, highlighting the characters featured in the series. It emphasizes the broad range of Lanterns that will appear in the adaptation.

title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 223 — The Lunar Domain
summary: The latest episode of 'This Week In Space' podcast discusses the future of lunar exploration with guest Dr. Scott Pace. The conversation focuses on the potential developments and challenges in the emerging lunar domain.

title: Firefly promote next block of Alpha amid Eclipse progress
summary: Firefly Aerospace is advancing its next-generation medium-lift rocket while also promoting its upcoming Alpha rocket block. The company is making progress on both fronts.

title: Blue Origin overviews plan for dual pad ops at Cape Canaveral
summary: Blue Origin is planning dual pad operations at Cape Canaveral as it restores its primary launch pad at LC-36A. The company has shared details about its operational expansion.

title: Rocket Lab advances via series of announcements
summary: Rocket Lab has established a new subsidiary in Germany and introduced a containerized mobile launch system. These moves are part of the company's expansion and technological advancements.

title: Amid failure, Wenchang celebrates milestone as China launches AI satellites and prepares for lunar south pole mission
summary: China's Wenchang Space Launch Site celebrated its 50th launch milestone while also experiencing a failure. The site launched AI satellites and is preparing for a lunar south pole mission.

title: Starbase Production lining up future vehicles
summary: SpaceX's Starbase production site is advancing the assembly of multiple Starship vehicles. This indicates ongoing preparations for future missions and production scaling at the facility.

title: Launch Preview: Chinese failure opens busy international launch salvo
summary: The week of August 10 began with four launches across three countries, following a Chinese failure. The busy international launch schedule highlights a competitive space industry.

title: Artemis progress building lunar return roadmap
summary: NASA has provided updates on the Artemis program, detailing progress in building a roadmap for returning humans to the Moon. The updates include plans for commercial robotic lunar missions.

title: Blue Origin working engine resolutions and dual pad future
summary: Blue Origin is nearing the end of its investigation into a catastrophic engine explosion. The company is also planning for a dual-pad future.

title: Relativity Space engine integration milestone for Terran-R first stage
summary: Relativity Space has achieved a key milestone in integrating engines for the first stage of its reusable Terran-R rocket. This marks progress in the development of their next-generation launch vehicle.

title: Crew-13 pilot reflects on career, training, and upcoming science ahead of flight to ISS
summary: NASA has moved up the launch date for the Crew-13 mission to the ISS, and the pilot has shared reflections on their career, training, and the upcoming science mission.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates its 50th anniversary with a booklet highlighting 50 key achievements over the past five decades. The publication underscores the agency's contributions to space exploration and technology.

title: Proba-3’s eclipse hours before totality in Europe
summary: Proba-3 mission will create an artificial solar eclipse hours before the total solar eclipse in Europe. This mission aims to study the Sun's corona by blocking out direct sunlight.

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3 will experience a double eclipse as the Moon crosses its field of view. This event highlights the satellite's precise orbital alignment.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and computer simulations to observe the Sun's corona. This effort is crucial for advancing solar science despite the rarity and brief duration of natural eclipses.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: ESA is inviting European researchers and companies to run software aboard the Hera asteroid mission in deep space. This offers a unique opportunity for testing software millions of kilometers from Earth.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESA's ESTEC technical center in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will demonstrate formation flying with two satellites to create an artificial solar eclipse using a coronagraph. The mission aims to study the Sun's corona by blocking the solar disk.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will showcase innovative space startups and foster collaboration with Europe's space industry on September 16-17 at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: The article discusses advancements in silicon-based technology for next-generation antennas. These innovations are expected to enhance performance and efficiency in space communications.

title: The New Middle Ground in Spacecraft Development
summary: The commercial space industry is shifting towards customers building their own spacecraft hardware for full mission ownership, moving beyond affordability and accessibility. This trend reflects a new demand for customization and control in spacecraft development.

title: Exclusive: Reflect Orbital Responds to its Critics
summary: Reflect Orbital faces criticism over its sunlight-reflecting satellites, sparking debate in the space community. The company has responded to these concerns.

title: NASA Opens Call on Moon Base Health Research
summary: NASA's Human Research Program is soliciting research proposals to address health concerns for long-term stays at a future Moon base. The initiative aims to gather insights to support sustainable human presence on the lunar surface.

title: Rocket Lab Enters Europe’s Crowded Launch Market
summary: Rocket Lab is entering Europe's competitive launch market, surprising local companies as they return from holiday. The move marks Rocket Lab's expansion into a new regional market.

title: Exclusive: Space Kinetic Awarded $50M for Space Maneuverability
summary: Space Kinetic secured a $50 million OTA award from the U.S. Space Force to develop Whirlwind, a space maneuverability and deployment system. This funding highlights the growing investment in space technology and maneuverability capabilities.

title: How to Pitch the Space Force: Green and Red Flags
summary: A Space Force official shared insights on how startups should pitch for award opportunities, highlighting green and red flags in applications. The discussion aims to improve startup engagement with the Space Force.

title: Astranis Unveils Perceptor, an SDA Product for GEO
summary: Astranis developed Perceptor, an SDA product designed to address issues with existing space domain awareness (SDA) technology while operating in geostationary orbit (GEO). The new tool aims to enhance SDA capabilities for GEO operations.

title: Firefly Announces Record Q2 Results
summary: Firefly Aerospace reported its first-ever quarterly revenue exceeding $100 million, driven by new launch and defense contracts. The company's Q2 results highlight significant growth in its space industry operations.

title: Guetlein: CR Could Mean ‘No Golden Dome…No Funding’
summary: A senior official warns that without a budget agreement, critical space programs may face funding shortages. The absence of a Continuing Resolution (CR) could lead to significant financial constraints.

title: Bill Spotlight: Space Superiority Readiness Act
summary: A bipartisan pair of senators introduced a bill to ensure U.S. military readiness for potential orbital conflicts with China. The legislation aims to enhance space superiority capabilities.

title: Space Force Awards Space Data Network Contracts to Five Satellite Manufacturers
summary: The U.S. Space Force has awarded contracts to five satellite manufacturers to develop a more diverse multi-vendor architecture for its space data network. This move aims to enhance the resilience and capabilities of the military's space-based communications.

title: Astranis Unveils Perceptor Space Domain Awareness GEO Satellite
summary: Astranis announced the unveiling of its new 'Perceptor' satellite designed for space domain awareness and maneuverability in GEO orbit. This marks Astranis' latest expansion into specialized satellite offerings.

title: CesiumAstro Acquires Semiconductor Company Jariet Technologies
summary: CesiumAstro has acquired Jariet Technologies, a semiconductor company, to enhance its communications and sensing systems for commercial, civil, and national security markets.

title: Planet Labs to Support Government, Public Services in Rwanda
summary: The Rwanda Government is partnering with Planet Labs to launch a new national program leveraging satellite technology for government and public services. This collaboration aims to enhance Rwanda's capabilities in utilizing satellite data for various applications.

title: Mantis Space Appoints Ex-Boeing Exec as CTO
summary: Mantis Space has appointed Dale Parkes, a former Boeing executive, as its new Chief Technology Officer. The appointment coincides with the company's efforts to develop a constellation of spacecraft for continuous Earth orbit operations.

title: Impulse Space Wins New Space Force Contract
summary: Impulse Space has secured a $28 million SBIR Phase III contract extension from the U.S. Space Force to support two missions. This marks further collaboration between the company and the Space Force.

title: Telesat Remains Optimistic About Lightspeed Despite Shaky 1H26 Financial Results, Looming Debt
summary: Telesat, a Canadian satellite operator, reported weak financial results for the first half of 2026 and faces concerns over upcoming debt maturity, but remains optimistic about its Lightspeed satellite constellation project.

title: Optus Completes First Part of Project Aurora
summary: Optus, an Australian telecommunications and satellite company, has completed the first phase of Project Aurora, a satellite life extension initiative. This milestone marks progress in extending the operational lifespan of its satellites.

title: Marlink to Acquire U.K. Defense Comms Specialist GRC
summary: Marlink is acquiring U.K.-based defense communications specialist GRC to strengthen its position in European government, defense, and critical infrastructure markets.

title: Space42 and Leonardo DRS to Boost UAE National Security
summary: Space42 and Leonardo DRS have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to enhance national security capabilities in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The agreement focuses on leveraging Leonardo DRS's expertise to support Space42's initiatives.
